newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean union agrees to TV debate.
newsitem.headline: South Korean union agrees to TV debate.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed umbrella union group said on Friday it would accept an offer to hold a televised debate with the ruling party over a controversial labour law.

"This is not engaging in official dialogue. We are agreeing to a TV debate to tell the public what is really going on," Yoon Young-mo, International Director of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, told reporters.
Ruling party chairman Lee Hong-koo has offered to debate union leaders spearheading more than three weeks of wildcat strikes.
Yoon said confederation president Kwon Young-kil would take part on condition it was broadcast live "so they can't edit it". No date had been proposed.
Arrest warrants have been issued for Kwon and six deputies sheltering at Seoul's Myongdong Cathedral.
"It would be silly for the government to arrest them on the way to the debate," Yoon said.
